summary.text: Rose Lounsbury is the Democratic candidate for Ohio House of Representatives District 36 in the November 3, 2026 general election, in a rematch with incumbent Republican Andrea White.
A former public school teacher and consultant, she has been affiliated with the League of Women Voters.

paragraphs.text: Rose Lounsbury earned a bachelor's degree from Western Michigan University in 2004 and a master's degree in teaching English language and literature from Miami University in 2008.
In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as a former public school teacher, small business owner and mother of teenage triplets who moved to Dayton about 20 years earlier.
She said she joined the League of Women Voters, where she served on its Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion committee, and was inspired to run for the State House in 2024.
Lounsbury won the March 19, 2024 Democratic primary for District 36 over Chuck Horn, then lost the November 5, 2024 general election to White, 52.4 percent to 47.6 percent.
Her 2024 survey listed protecting democracy, ending gerrymandering, women's rights, public education, health care and gun safety among her priorities.
